maths-net-tool — Quick Guide

Dyslexia-friendly reading view

🚀 How to Open maths-net-tool

Double-click maths-net-tool.html or index.html in any browser. It runs 100% offline on computers, tablets, and school interactive whiteboards.

🎮 Moving & Folding in 3D

Rotate: Left-click & drag (or 1 finger)
Move: Right-click & drag (or 2 fingers)
Zoom: Scroll wheel (or pinch)
Fold: Drag slider 0% to 100%
Play: Click ▶ Play or ⏸ Pause
Auto-Pause: Pauses on tab switch

🧭 The Three Workspaces in maths-net-tool

🔍 Mode 1: Explore Shapes

Pick from 15 shapes and nets. Use the slider to fold them in 3D. Overlapping faces in invalid nets turn bright red.

✏️ Mode 2: Draw a Net

Click squares on the 7×7 grid to place 6 squares. Click Test Fold to see if it makes a cube without collisions.

🧩 Mode 3: Shape Matcher

Use ‹ and › to choose a shape. Drag faces onto the workbench—they magnetically snap edge-to-edge. Click Clue for hints, then fold it in 3D!

🛠️ Helpful Exam Tools in maths-net-tool

  • 🎯 Opposite Faces Quiz: Practice finding opposite faces without folding—a common Functional Skills question.
  • 📊 Surface Area: Type in your measurements to see step-by-step surface area calculations.
  • 🖨️ Print Net Templates: Create clean A4 worksheets (1 or 2 nets per page) with no black borders, ready to cut and fold.

📝 Four Key Exam Rules

Rule 1: Count the Faces — Cube has 6, Triangular Prism has 5, Square Pyramid has 5, Tetrahedron has 4.
Rule 2: No 2×2 Blocks — 4 squares forming a 2×2 square always collide and fail to make a cube.
Rule 3: Opposite Faces Never Touch — Opposite faces in 3D never share an edge on the flat net.
Rule 4: The 1-4-1 Pattern — A row of 4 with 1 on each side always folds into a valid cube or cuboid.

🎯 Opposite Faces Challenge (FS Exam Skill)

On this cube net, the Bottom face (Base) is shaded Blue. Which face will be directly opposite it when the net is fully folded into a cube?

📊 Surface Area from Nets (L1 & L2)

In Functional Skills exams, surface area is calculated by adding the areas of each 2D face in the net.

Total Surface Area = 24 cm²
